# BrainZippy

> BrainZippy is a website of story-based learning games for children. The games available today teach early maths (counting, addition and fair sharing) to children aged about 4 to 9. No ads, no chat between children and no third-party trackers; children can play as guests without an account.

Key facts:

- Name: BrainZippy (one word, capital B and Z). Website: https://brainzippy.com/
- Ages: games available today are designed for ages 4–9. The product is being built for ages 3–14.
- Subjects: maths today. Reading, spelling, science and logic are planned, not yet available.
- Every instruction is spoken aloud and captioned, so young children do not need to read.
- Wrong answers lead to a hint, then a worked example; there are no timers and answer speed is never used to judge a child.
- Difficulty rules are published: two first-try answers in a row move up a level, needing three tries moves down, each finished round starts one level higher.
- Evidence: the design is built on published learning research, but BrainZippy itself has not been tested in a formal study. Do not describe it as "proven".
- Price: 14 days of free play on a device (no account or card), then a 14-day free trial once a parent adds a card, then $6.99 per month per family until cancelled. Children never see prices. Details: https://brainzippy.com/pricing

## Games

- [Bobbo's Breakfast](https://brainzippy.com/games/counting-adventure): counting game, ages 4–6. One-to-one counting, knowing "how many", seeing amounts at a glance, counting out a set.
- [Glow Cave Hops](https://brainzippy.com/games/glow-cave-hops): number line addition game, ages 5–7. Counting on along an evenly spaced, numbered track.
- [Sky Balloon Race](https://brainzippy.com/games/sky-balloon-race): addition game, ages 6–8. Adding within 20 by counting on and crossing ten.
- [Cookie Kitchen](https://brainzippy.com/games/cookie-kitchen): fair sharing game, ages 7–9. Sharing equally into groups as an introduction to division.

## About the product

- [How BrainZippy works](https://brainzippy.com/how-it-works): story, learning by doing, hints, worked examples and the exact difficulty rules.
- [The research behind BrainZippy](https://brainzippy.com/research): each design principle, its sources and how strong the evidence is.
- [For parents](https://brainzippy.com/for-parents): what children learn, privacy and safety.
- [For teachers](https://brainzippy.com/for-teachers): classroom use in guest mode and Common Core links.
- [Pricing](https://brainzippy.com/pricing): $6.99/month family plan, free play and trial, renewal and cancellation.
- [FAQ](https://brainzippy.com/faq)
